fact_sheet.business_description: The Company connects consumers with local merchants through discounted offers and operates Goods activities [D01]. It is attempting a turnaround focused on improving local-commerce activity and operating leverage, characterized as a repeat local-commerce network rather than a traditional inventory retailer [D01].
segments_and_separable_assets: Local-commerce network: Identified as the core turnaround focus with $1.49bn in Q2 2016 gross billings; North American Local billings grew 9% [D03].
Goods activities: Operates alongside Local offerings; performance metrics are not broken out independently from the aggregate [D01, D05].
Available cash: $780.1m cash as of June 30, 2016, though this contains merchant settlement working capital [D04].
economics_vs_peers: Revenue growth: 2.4% (Q2 2016) vs eBay -2.3% (FY2015), Amazon 20.2% (FY2015), TripAdvisor 19.7% (FY2015) [D06].
Operating margin: -5.7% (Q2 2016) vs eBay 25.6% (FY2015), Amazon 2.1% (FY2015), TripAdvisor 15.5% (FY2015) [D06].
Margin gap: Not in pack; accounting perimeters differ between gross physical-goods sales and net service commissions [D06].
capital_structure: Leverage: Net cash approximately $530.1m (Equity plus notes less cash) [D04].
Other: Merchant settlement working capital and customer advances are present [D02, D04].
price_and_valuation: FCF yield: Approximately 5.75% based on FY2015 CFO less capex [D04].

final.memo:
The Company is currently attempting an internal operational turnaround focused on its local-commerce network, yet we see no mispricing or event-driven catalyst to support an investment [D01]. The business represents a secularly challenged consumer-internet model where the path to profitability remains entirely unproven [D01, D05].

Financially, the company remains distressed with an operating margin of -5.7% (Q2 2016), lagging significantly behind peers like eBay, which maintains a 25.6% operating margin [D06]. While the company holds $780.1m in cash, this balance is offset by $250m in convertible debt and heavy working capital requirements [D04].

Market concerns regarding the durability of the model are well-founded, as increased marketing expenditures appear to drive transient traffic rather than loyal, recurring engagement [D05]. Without separable assets or a defined path to structural simplification, we are left betting on a multi-year management execution plan that lacks a governance anchor [D01, D07].

We have no role in this process and no leverage to force change. The lack of a clear catalyst and the reliance on an unproven turnaround makes the risk/reward profile unattractive. We have decided to PASS and will allocate our capital to opportunities with a more identifiable margin of safety and a defined path to value realization [D01, D08].
